hints: The sample mean is the unbiased estimate of the population mean: add up the 10 heights and divide by $n = 10$.

For an unbiased estimate of the variance use $s^2 = \dfrac{1}{n-1}\left(\Sigma x^2 - \dfrac{(\Sigma x)^2}{n}\right)$ with $n = 10$. First square each of the 10 heights and add the squares to get $\Sigma x^2$.
Put your $\Sigma x^2$ and $\Sigma x$ into the formula and divide by $9$, not $10$ (dividing by $10$ gives the biased version). Give the answer to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
**What we are asked**

We only have a **sample** of 10 trees, not every tree of this variety. So we use the sample to make **unbiased estimates**: estimates that are right on average.

$n = 10$ is the number of trees. $\Sigma x$ means "add up all the heights" and $\Sigma x^2$ means "square each height first, then add up the squares".

**Estimate of the population mean (B1)**

The best estimate of the population mean is the sample mean $\bar{x}$ (read "x bar"): the total of the heights divided by the number of trees.

Add the heights one at a time:

$$5.9 + 6.5 = 12.4,\quad 12.4 + 6.7 = 19.1,\quad 19.1 + 5.9 = 25.0,\quad 25.0 + 6.9 = 31.9$$

$$31.9 + 6.0 = 37.9,\quad 37.9 + 6.4 = 44.3,\quad 44.3 + 6.2 = 50.5,\quad 50.5 + 5.8 = 56.3,\quad 56.3 + 5.8 = 62.1$$

So $\Sigma x = 62.1$. Now divide by $10$:

$$\bar{x} = \frac{62.1}{10} = 6.21$$

This earns the B1.

**Work out the sum of the squares**

For the variance we also need $\Sigma x^2$. Square each height (calculator: type the number, then $x^2$):

$$5.9^2 = 34.81,\quad 6.5^2 = 42.25,\quad 6.7^2 = 44.89,\quad 5.9^2 = 34.81,\quad 6.9^2 = 47.61$$

$$6.0^2 = 36,\quad 6.4^2 = 40.96,\quad 6.2^2 = 38.44,\quad 5.8^2 = 33.64,\quad 5.8^2 = 33.64$$

Add them one at a time:

$$34.81 + 42.25 = 77.06,\quad 77.06 + 44.89 = 121.95,\quad 121.95 + 34.81 = 156.76,\quad 156.76 + 47.61 = 204.37$$

$$204.37 + 36 = 240.37,\quad 240.37 + 40.96 = 281.33,\quad 281.33 + 38.44 = 319.77,\quad 319.77 + 33.64 = 353.41,\quad 353.41 + 33.64 = 387.05$$

$$\Sigma x^2 = 387.05$$

Quick check: your calculator's statistics mode should give the same $\Sigma x$ and $\Sigma x^2$.

**Choose the unbiased variance formula (M1)**

A sample is a little less spread out than the whole population, so dividing by $n$ gives an estimate that is slightly too small. Dividing by $n - 1 = 9$ corrects this. The unbiased estimate is $s^2$:

$$s^2 = \frac{1}{n-1}\left(\Sigma x^2 - \frac{(\Sigma x)^2}{n}\right) = \frac{1}{9}\left(387.05 - \frac{62.1^2}{10}\right)$$

The scheme also accepts $\dfrac{10}{9}\left(\dfrac{387.05}{10} - 6.21^2\right)$, which is the same calculation written another way. Writing either expression with your numbers earns the M1.

**Calculate it one piece at a time (A1)**

Square the total: $62.1^2 = 3856.41$.

Divide by $10$: $\dfrac{3856.41}{10} = 385.641$.

Subtract from $\Sigma x^2$: $387.05 - 385.641 = 1.409$.

Divide by $9$:

$$s^2 = \frac{1.409}{9} = 0.15655\ldots = 0.157 \text{ (3 s.f.)}$$

Common slip: dividing $1.409$ by $10$ gives $0.1409$, the **biased** variance. The scheme gives M0 for that.

**Final answer**

Unbiased estimate of the population mean: $6.21$ metres.

Unbiased estimate of the population variance: $0.157$ (3 s.f.), which is $\dfrac{1409}{9000}$ exactly.
